page.layout: One printed page of running text, full width. Running head at the top, centred, with the page number at the top right. At the foot: the signature "Cc 6" under the text, and "EPIST." at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: qvibus devotum illi obseqvium meum testarer, credidi tamen officii mei esse R. Patre Goezaldo Romam redeunte eum hinc abire insalutata Eminentia vestra non finere ; Cùm enim ei sit a multis annis cognitus, eumqve sæpius colloqvio suo benigne honoraverit, literas meas merito deferentis illi gratiores fore existimavi. Religio mihi est,& quidem verecundus pudor Eminentiam vestram rebus arduis occupatissimam interpellare, & dum mente versat, & disponit negotia totius orbis Christiani maxima & difficillima,mei homuncionis plane inutilis mentionem injicere. Sed cùm in memoriā revoco eā qva me semper complexus es benevolentiam,cujꝰ argumenta qvam plurima mihi dedisti,animū & confidentiā resumo,mihiq; persuadeo,frequens obseqvii mei testimonium. Eminentiae vestrae non fore importunū.
Vale Eminentissime Cardinalis. Deus Eminentiam vestram incolumenEcclesiae quàm diutissime conservet.
Parisiis viij. Id. Octob. Anno MDCLIII.

page.notes: Transcribed from the scan; the printed "sem-per", "ar-gumenta", "ani-mū" and "persua-deo" hyphens at line ends are kept. Printed spellings left as they are: "qva", "qvam", "obseqvium", "incolumenEcclesiae" (missing space), "difponit", "interpellare". The date uses the reversed-C numerals CIↃ IↃCLIII, given as MDCLIII. The "cujꝰ" glyph is uncertain and could be a different -us abbreviation. Where the printed text is smeared, "importunū" and "impoꝛtunū" are close together; I read "importunū".
